To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the number of NEAs is 981 ± 18 for D > 1 km and that the number of D > 100 m NEAs is 20,500±3000.
the NEOWISE survey has detected 428 NEAs, that 981 ± 21 NEAs larger than ~1 km exist, and that 13,200 ±1900 NEAs are larger than 140 m.
the cumulative size frequency distribution of the NEA population is a broken power law that has a slope of 0.68 ± 0.03 above 1.5-2.0 km and a slope of 2.32 ± 1.4 below that size.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the number and size of the NEO population.
the discovery and characterization of NEOs and their populations and the use of this information to better understand the nature of the NEO population.
the determination of physical properties of NEOs, including their diameters, albedos, and the thermal properties of their surfaces.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the NEO population has been well-characterized, with a few remaining gaps that will be addressed in future surveys, such as NEOWISE's ongoing post-cryogenic mission.

we have detected 90% of the 1 km diameter NEAs, but the number of 500 meter diameter NEAs is still a factor of two larger than the NEOWISE number, and that there is a factor of 10 uncertainty in the total number of 100 meter diameter NEAs.
the NEO population has been well characterized and that the risk from impact by a large object is very small.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the number of NEAs is lower than previously thought, but that their albedos are higher, so the total mass is similar.
we have detected ~90% of the 1 km NEA population, ~50% of the 500 m NEA population, and ~20% of the 200 m NEA population.
the NEO population is well described by a broken power-law size distribution with a break point at 1.5 ± 0.5 km, and a power-law index of 1.5-1.7 above the break and 1.3 ± 0.1 below it.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the NEO population is better characterized than any other asteroid population in the Solar System, and we have identified some of the most important remaining questions about this population.
we have a good understanding of the size distribution of NEAs, but the albedo distribution remains a major uncertainty.
the WISE survey has provided an excellent census of the NEO population.
